# Agent Harness Evaluations

Local coding-agent comparisons using pinned [Inspect AI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/).
Inspect owns evaluation execution, Docker sandbox lifecycle, scoring and logs.
The repository supplies native-product adapters, research/account policy,
independent task verification and experiment definitions.

The current benchmark is the [staged MultiLang v5 contract](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md):
a 25-task, seven-arm Stage A, followed by a separately frozen Stage B with
surviving standard arms, Pi and RelayView. See the [delivery roadmap](docs/contracts/unified-benchmark-roadmap.md).
A complete comparative Stage A has not yet been published.

## Current execution

Five-project operational qualification and Stage A share
`stage_a_execution.execute_attempt`: native execution, sanitized task preparation,
terminal candidate capture, quiescence, independent verification, retained Inspect
evidence and task-outcome-v2 normalization. Task-specific verification differs:
SWE-bench's five Python projects use their pinned commands/parser; MultiLang uses
its pinned language-specific commands and separate parser environment.

- [Current five-project qualification and retirement guide](docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md)
- [Stage A freeze and execution](docs/runbooks/multilang-stage-a-freeze.md)
- [Scoped Inspect recovery](docs/runbooks/inspect-recovery-and-shakedown.md)
- [Current outcome contract](docs/contracts/task-outcomes-v2.md)

Qualification is a seven-arm × five-task operational check, separate from
comparative results. Issue #180’s live gate completed with all 35 outcomes
recorded and audited; see the [final evidence and investigation dispositions](docs/evidence/current-qualification-180-final.md).
The 31 passes, three verifier failures and one timeout are operational evidence
across documented repair revisions, not a comparative Stage A ranking.

Historical pilot, pair-shakedown and conformance-matrix orchestration and older
benchmark validators are retired at HEAD. Existing evidence remains unchanged.
Use the source revision recorded with a historical run to reproduce its commands;
Git retains those implementations. Current deterministic native conformance,
research admission, Pi and RelayView adapters remain supported.

## Install

Use Linux, Python 3.12+, Node 22.19+ and Docker/Compose. The repository pins
Inspect AI 0.3.261 and Inspect Evals 0.16.0. Its dependency commands require uv
0.12.9; if the host uv differs, use `uvx --from uv==0.12.9 uv` in place of `uv`.

```sh
uv sync --locked
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

The independently pinned Codex/Muse runtime requires the existing
[build/install procedure](docs/runbooks/codex-muse-runtime.md).
Do not replace it with stock Codex. Dependencies must be available inside the
checkout mounted by Docker; symlinking `node_modules` outside it is insufficient.

## Provider-free checks

```sh
uv run --locked python -m pytest -q tests/test_shakedown_matrix.py tests/test_qualification_inputs.py -m 'not benchmark_docker'
uv run --locked python scripts/package_swe_bench_tasks.py --check
uv run --locked python scripts/run_shakedown_matrix.py --help
```

The qualification runbook lists native/Inspect/recovery checks and the explicit
Docker gold/unchanged controls. `make check` remains the full repository gate;
use focused checks while developing a bounded change. Neither mock credentials
nor provider-free tests authorize a live run.

## Native products and research

- [Native research clients and probes](docs/runbooks/native-research-clients.md)
- [OpenCode adapter](docs/runbooks/opencode-adapter.md)
- [Claude Code adapter](docs/runbooks/claude-code-adapter.md)
- [Pi baseline adapter](docs/runbooks/pi-standard-adapter.md)
- [RelayView owner adapter](docs/runbooks/relayview-owner-adapter.md)
- [Shared research service](docs/runbooks/shared-research-service.md)

Current Stage A and qualification use controlled GitHub-excluded research with
[shared budget v2](docs/contracts/shared-research-budget-v2.md). Each native CLI
retains its declared provider/subscription route. Inspect model proxies and
agent bridges are outside this experiment's measurement boundary.

Provider credentials remain bounded runtime inputs. Current admission must bind
actual runtime, tools, routes and source revision. Cleanup does not refund spent
quota, replay interrupted native work, or turn a missing verifier result into a
capability zero.

66	itself: `--for-execution` remains fail-closed until #50 evidence and #23/#24
67	enforcement exist.
68	Issue #24 must supply the Stage A `purpose=freeze` manifest on the reviewed
69	archive-bound corpus (23 tasks, ADR-0016), and #50 the later disjoint Stage B
70	corpus. Each needs exact admitted identities and real approval/evidence digests
71	before #23/#24 may consume it.
72	
73	## Purpose and fair product comparison
74	
75	The primary benchmark supports honest product marketing: how recognizable developer
76	configurations compare on coding outcomes, latency and resources. RelayView may be
77	valuable by preserving coding quality while adding separately demonstrated
78	governance, provenance, safe recovery and human-review benefits. No AGI claim or
79	unexplained composite score follows from this experiment.
80	
81	Fairness means identical task/scorer inputs and disclosed, prospectively frozen
82	conditions—not identical tools. Preserve each product's useful native capabilities
83	and equivalents. Do not transplant RelayView-specialized memory, AST/LSP/code
84	intelligence, expert escalation, separate planner/implementer roles or auto-review
85	into Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code or standard Pi just to equalize them. Do not cripple competing
86	products by removing native equivalents.
87	
88	The shared broker, disabled native research routes and GitHub-family exclusions
89	are deliberate controls that change the native experience. Report them; do not
90	claim these are untouched stock profiles. This amendment does not undo those
91	controls, change normal non-benchmark defaults or permit ad hoc source exceptions.
92	
93	## Invariants
94	
95	- A cohort is identified by immutable corpus, arm-set, policy, scheduler, scorer
96	  and resource digests. Resume rejects any mismatch.
97	- Every task input, source/setup revision, environment image digest, verifier and
98	  scorer is identical across the arms in that cohort.
99	- One trial is one arm-task-repetition slot. Every scheduled slot is reconciled as
100	  valid capability evidence, infrastructure missing, unsupported or unstarted.
101	- Primary task outcome incorporates eligible within-budget delivery and independent
102	  terminal-candidate verification. Preserve the verifier observation separately:
103	  an eligible task timeout remains primary zero even if a retained patch passes.
104	  Automated/human dispositions are separate; initial/reviewed RelayView candidates
105	  are paired secondary checkpoints, not additional arms.
106	- Capability results never select or replace tasks. Hidden verifier material and
107	  scores remain unavailable until automatic work has stopped and cannot feed a
108	  later role or retry.
109	- Research profiles, model/provider routes, prompts, deadlines, attempts and
110	  budgets are frozen prospectively. The shared research budget v2 applies. All
111	  seven Stage A arms use the controlled researcher under
112	  [`github-excluded-v1`](github-excluded-research-v1.md); public-web or native
113	  search evidence does not admit this cohort.
114	- Screening, expansion, pilot, shakedown and conformance evidence are never pooled.
115	
116	## Stage A — screening cohort
117	
118	The arm set is exactly the seven standard arms listed in ADR-0012. RelayView is not
119	part of this cohort and its delivery or admission cannot block Stage A.
120	
121	The seventh arm is `claude-code-claude-opus-5`, frozen by the
122	[Claude Code subscription baseline](../authoritative/claude-code-subscription-baseline.md).
123	It uses Claude Code 2.1.270, full-name `claude-opus-5`, high effort, the Anthropic
124	subscription route, native prompt and repository instruction discovery, one
125	primary coding agent, an exact native tool inventory, and only the controlled
126	research MCP pair. The `Agent`, `Workflow`, agent-team, native web/search and
127	alternate research paths are disabled. Any alias, fallback, package, route,
128	tool, prompt-discovery, output, deadline or retry drift creates a different arm.
129	
130	Every Stage A launcher explicitly selects `--github-excluded`. The default
131	`public-web-v1` remains available for non-benchmark work but is inadmissible for
132	this cohort. Codex/GPT-5.6 Sol disables native OpenAI search only in its generated
133	benchmark profile and receives the same broker tools as the other six arms. All
134	six legacy arms require fresh live admission under issue #116 before task delivery;
135	the Claude arm requires its own fresh exact-identity admission before task delivery. Historical
136	#73/#98-#102 evidence remains operational history rather than current admission.
137	The immutable seven-record index binds the exact retained matrix, per-arm evidence,
138	deployment/setup identities and common controlled-service identity. A Stage A
139	freeze records that index as `source_policy.research_admission_digest`; changing
140	or omitting it creates an incompatible freeze and blocks dispatch.
141	
142	Issue #50 selected 25 validated tasks from a content-addressed revision of
143	`SWE-bench-Live/MultiLang`; the executable Stage A corpus is the reviewed
144	subset of that selection defined below. The current candidate dataset revision is
145	`62dc0745c40f067fc366ae3eb1a26136e5928f85`; #50 must independently verify it and
146	must not substitute a mutable branch or `latest` reference. Candidate tasks have
147	`created_at >= 2026-04-01`, after #50 verifies whether that field represents the
148	source issue or pull-request time and records the underlying source timestamp.
149	At that candidate revision the date filter yields 512 rows (C 77, C++ 100, Go 36,
150	JavaScript 22, Rust 101, Java 81, TypeScript 15 and C# 80); #50 must reproduce the
151	inventory before treating it as freeze input.
152	
153	The selection algorithm is frozen before capability outcomes:
154	
155	1. Validate eligibility, environment reproducibility, base/no-op behavior, the
156	   gold patch repeatedly, verifier isolation, problem/test alignment and the
157	   supported host/resource envelope.
158	2. Freeze the exact selection allocation. The original was `c=3`, `cpp=3`,
159	   `go=3`, `js=3`, `rust=3`, `java=3`, `ts=3`, `cs=4`; the selection that
160	   produced the archived tasks used ADR-0015's `c=3`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`, `js=3`,
161	   `rust=3`, `java=0`, `ts=4`, `cs=4`.
162	3. Within each language, retain only the newest eligible task per repository,
163	   then order tasks by the ISO `created_at` value descending and `instance_id`
164	   ascending using bytewise comparison. Select the allocation from the head of
165	   each order. The selected tasks must come from distinct repositories.
166	4. Freeze the remaining per-language order as the replacement list. A replacement
167	   stays in the same language and uses the next unused repository. It is allowed
168	   only for a predeclared validation failure discovered before any comparative
169	   outcome, never for difficulty or an arm outcome, and creates a new corpus
170	   revision. After the first trial begins, no task replacement is permitted.
171	   A task that later leaves the eligible set is dropped, not replaced; the
172	   change creates a new corpus identity and a smaller schedule.
173	
174	The executable Stage A corpus is the reviewed subset of the full task-archive
175	release: 23 tasks from 23 repositories, allocation `c=2`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`,
176	`js=3`, `rust=2`, `java=0`, `ts=4`, `cs=4`. Archive review left
177	`AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` and `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180` `unresolved`; both are
178	dropped without replacement. Each retained task keeps its selected task ID,
179	source revision and task text and is graded by its reviewed validator. Reports
180	disclose the reduced C and Rust strata and the absence of Java.
181	
182	MultiLang does not publish a separate per-row ingestion timestamp. #50 must prove
183	the semantics and normalization of `created_at` before it becomes the recency key;
184	if that proof fails, the freeze is blocked pending a new owner decision. Applied
185	to the unvalidated pinned inventory, this rule's projected oldest selected value
186	is `2026-04-17T03:18:51Z` (`danielmiessler__Fabric-2098`, Go). The projection is
187	planning evidence, not a frozen task: validation may move the final oldest date
188	earlier while preserving the exact language and repository allocation.
189	
190	The MultiLang adapter is part of the measuring instrument and must consume each
191	task's declared rebuild/test/print commands, log parser and image. It must discover
192	the repository root rather than assume `/testbed/.git`, safely isolate untrusted
193	parser/test execution, support compiled-language resource needs, pin images by
194	digest and emit typed failures. Existing Python/Inspect scorer evidence does not
195	admit this adapter. #50 records the exact adapter, evaluator and schema versions
196	and fresh validation evidence.
197	
198	The scheduler creates seeded task/repetition blocks containing exactly all seven
199	arms. It may execute sequentially and may defer a quota-blocked slot within a
200	block, but cannot omit it or begin a later block early.
201	
202	Stage A runs every block in schedule order from one ledger under one admitted
203	configuration and the owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of that freeze
204	is the only launch decision. The cohort has no first-block stop and no owner
205	go/no-go between blocks. Each block runs under the admitted per-block
206	supervisor watchdog. After a block completes cleanly, the launcher
207	automatically starts the next block from the same ledger under the same
208	supervisor policy, with no operator action. A block that does not complete
209	cleanly, including a watchdog stop, stops the cohort fail-closed. An uncertain
210	or active attempt is never replayed, the ledger is never reset, and an
211	infrastructure stop retains the ledger and evidence for diagnosis. Resuming
212	the same ledger requires the same admitted configuration and is a recovery,
213	not a new approval.
214	
215	The Claude arm's enrollment receipt must cover each pending Claude turn under
216	the frozen phase limits. An authenticated renewal during the run is a recorded
217	operator recovery, not an owner decision. It keeps the same account, token,
218	tier and credit/isolation settings and authenticates against the frozen
219	identities. It carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation and adds no
220	reservation or refund. It never extends or overwrites the original receipt,
221	and it is bound into the ledger and evidence. Without a valid renewal, a
222	pending turn the receipt cannot cover fails closed before reservation, and a
223	renewal with a changed identity is rejected.
224	
225	After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit covers
226	all scheduled slots, including every renewal's chronology, before #24 seals
227	the cohort. The historical #155 and #220 first-block executions keep their own
228	stop, audit and owner decisions.
229	
230	The freeze declares
231	repetitions, the common total workflow deadline, retry policy, concurrency and
232	per-provider/account/local-compute reservations. Stage A freezes exactly one
233	repetition: one trial per arm-task pair, so the schedule has the frozen task
234	count × seven slots (161 for 23 tasks). This directional
235	screen identifies critically failing arms; it does not estimate run-to-run
236	reliability. A study of multiple tries requires a separately identified cohort,
237	predeclared aggregation and interpretation, and results that are not pooled with
238	Stage A.
239	
240	## Screening report and futility disposition
241	
242	Issue #24 seals Stage A independently. Issue #25 publishes all seven arms with
243	scheduled, attempted, valid, unsupported, infrastructure-missing and unstarted
244	denominators; per-task outcomes; all-scheduled lower/upper bounds; task-clustered
245	uncertainty; failure-inclusive time; research/provider/local resource use; and all
246	predeclared paired comparisons. It must say that one task is 1/23 of an arm's
247	denominator, about 4.35 percentage points, and must not present close ordering
248	as a precise ranking. Before publishing
249	the trusted disposition digest, #25 must validate each disposition record against
250	the independently trusted Stage A outcome seal and the sealed outcome records; the
251	Stage B validator authenticates both that published disposition and its referenced
252	source seal, but does not reinterpret the outcome records itself.
253	
254	No fixed number of arms is dropped. A standard arm is capability-futile only when
255	
256	`resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`
257	
258	after every one of its 23 scheduled task slots is reconciled. `capability_unknown`
259	includes every slot whose missingness could conceal a resolution. The rule is an
260	absolute resource stop, not statistical proof of general inferiority. An arm with
261	an upper bound of at least 2/23 survives. Failure to achieve frozen admission or
262	minimum valid coverage after the predeclared bounded attempts is reported as
263	`unsupported` and decided separately; it must not be described as capability
264	culling. Every disposition and its inputs are sealed as
265	`stage-a-capability-disposition/1`: one ordered record per scheduled Stage A
266	slot (161), carrying the frozen slot
267	ID, arm ID and one of `resolved`, `not_resolved`, `capability_unknown` or
268	`unstarted`, plus the Stage A freeze, outcome slot-plan and source outcome-seal
269	digests. The same calculation is performed independently for each of the seven
270	arms, including Claude Code; it cannot be omitted from the disposition input or
271	treated as an automatic survivor.
272	
273	## Stage B — selected-arm expansion cohort
274	
275	After the Stage A seal and report, #50 freezes a new corpus containing no Stage A
276	task. Prefer repository-disjointness from Stage A and development/shakedown exposure
277	where feasible, freeze exclusions before outcomes, and disclose unavoidable overlap.
278	The arm set is every surviving standard arm plus `relayview-sol`, `relayview-local`
279	and one standard single-agent Pi baseline under newly frozen exact identities.
280	RelayView production delivery (#64), Intel-successor exact-pair admission (#172), research readiness
281	(#68) and Pi adapter/admission (#130) gate Stage B only. A material configuration change to a
282	standard arm requires a new name and admission; it is not the same continuing arm.
283	
284	The owner freezes Stage B sample size, language/repository allocation, practical
285	thresholds, repetitions, resources and exact arm set after seeing the complete
286	Stage A report but before any Stage B outcome. Stage A may inform those prospective
287	choices. Stage B task selection may use only frozen metadata and validation, not
288	which Stage A tasks or arms succeeded. The cohort is described as
289	`<N>-arm selected expansion`, with three through ten arms; it is ten-arm only
290	when all seven standard arms survive. Standard Pi must not be silently omitted if
291	admission is unavailable: an altered arm set needs a new explicit owner decision.
292	
293	Issue #23 schedules the exact frozen Stage B arm set. #24 produces a separate seal.
294	#25 produces a separate expansion report and does not combine numerators,
295	denominators or uncertainty with Stage A. It discloses the selection procedure and
296	limits generalization accordingly. #66 analyzes RelayView's paired checkpoints
297	only from the Stage B seal and supplies that secondary analysis to the expansion
298	report.
299	
300	## Standard single-agent Pi
301	
302	[#129](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/129) pins the
303	[standard single-agent Pi baseline](../authoritative/pi-standard-baseline.md): Pi
304	0.85.0, `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`, ChatGPT OAuth, high reasoning, native prompt
305	and instruction discovery, one RPC-controlled agent, all seven Pi built-in coding
306	and search/list tools, and only the controlled research pair as a non-native
307	extension. [#130](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/130)
308	implements and admits that exact identity. No extra Pi-local arm is implicitly
309	approved.
310	
311	The capability inventory covers file read/edit/write, text/file search, shell,
312	tests/builds, interruption/deadlines/output bounds, repository instructions,
313	native context handling, provider features and admitted research. Distinguish native
314	tools, necessary benchmark capture/isolation/research adapters, optional commonplace
315	extensions and RelayView-specific enhancements. A practical baseline is not a claim
316	of identical capabilities or an intentionally weakened agent.
317	
318	Stage B prospectively freezes the existing shared-broker/GitHub-excluded treatment
319	for every selected arm, including Pi and RelayView, with fresh exact-policy admission.
320	Do not reinterpret old native/public-web evidence as admission. One workflow budget
321	covers every role/continuation/retry; reviewer research remains zero under the
322	existing policy. No additional memory/code-intelligence/assistance allowance is
323	introduced.
324	
325	## Outcome dimensions and evaluator integrity
326	
327	The implemented prospective [task outcome v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md) versions
328	verifier result, terminal reason, delivery-within-budget, primary task outcome/score
329	and applicable automated/human dispositions separately. The
330	[implemented timeout policy](../authoritative/task-budget-outcomes.md) remains:
331	eligible active-agent deadline timeout is primary zero, terminal and non-retryable.
332	A passing retained patch may separately have verifier pass. Setup/auth/provider/
333	capture/scorer failures and manual cancellation are not invented test failures.
334	Unknown identity/usage remains unknown. Specify combined-cause precedence and
335	eligibility deterministically before execution.
336	
337	Preserve upstream task/tests/evaluator semantics. #50 validates local integration
338	using repeated gold and base/no-op controls, the same patch through upstream and
339	integrated paths where feasible, correct rebuild instead of stale compiled output,
340	test discovery, setup/parser failures and candidate test tampering. Reuse existing
341	coverage. Supplemental behavioral tests are separately labeled diagnostics, never
342	silent changes to the official score.
343	
344	Historical logs, seals and original interpretations stay immutable. Any offline
345	reinterpretation identifies both original and successor policy; preserve the
346	disclosed after-observation adoption of the existing timeout policy.
347	
348	## Reporting, generalization and resource limits
349	
350	#25 publishes predeclared paired wins/losses, task-clustered uncertainty,
351	scheduled/attempted/valid/missing denominators, all-scheduled bounds and
352	failure-inclusive latency. Repetitions are not new independent repositories.
353	A 23-task screen changes about 4.35 percentage points per task; zero to four
354	examples per language cannot support language rankings. Recency-first selection is purposive,
355	not random; resampling does not cure that limitation. Dates do not establish
356	absence from pretraining, public mirrors or developer tuning.
357	
358	Disclose Stage A-informed selection/sizing and Stage B repository/development
359	overlap; describe familiar/new repositories separately when overlap is unavoidable.
360	“No significant difference” does not establish no degradation. Confirmatory
361	non-inferiority requires a predeclared tolerable margin, comparison, uncertainty
362	criterion and adequate sample/resources. Inconclusive results remain publishable.
363	
364	Freeze actual versus unavailable token/output/turn enforcement, all-role/provider
365	and research usage, workflow deadlines and local CPU/GPU/memory/concurrency limits.
366	Report cold/warm provisioning/cache effects and unknown metrics. Equal wall time
367	is not equal compute; subscription use is neither zero cost nor grounds for
368	inventing a per-task API price. Preserve account counters and reservations.
369	A finite cohort window, bounded operational attempts and resource-stop rules
370	prevent indefinite waiting. Unsupported admission is not capability-futility.
371	The retained upper-bound rule (at most one possible resolution, 1/23) is
372	near-total-failure screening, not a precise inferiority test or economical
373	arm-ranking procedure.
374	
375	GitHub exclusions block legitimate documentation including GitHub Pages and do not
376	prevent every solution exposure. Retain sanitized denial/filter diagnostics, not
377	blocked source content, and label restricted-source conditions. A realistic-docs
378	sensitivity cohort is optional later work, not a post-results exception.
379	
380	## Later feature attribution
381	
382	[#132](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/132) owns a
383	separate held-out RelayView-only ablation study after the first product baseline,
384	consuming [RelayView #446](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/pi-coding-agent-setup/issues/446).
385	Design may proceed earlier. Use a stripped RelayView control and prioritized
386	feature-specific contrasts as features ship; distinguish incremental from
387	full-minus-one designs and record interactions. Feature-off must remove execution/
388	tool admission and isolate mutable state. Reject impossible combinations or name
389	them as compound interventions; planner removal may alter reviewer snapshots too.
390	
391	Control task/model routes and total budgets, with comparable extra self-work where
392	feasible for review attribution. Initial/reviewed checkpoints alone measure
393	review-plus-correction, additional work and selection—not a reviewer-only causal
394	effect. Publish regressions and missingness. Hidden scores never guide agents,
395	escalation, retry or candidate choice.
396	
397	Do not transplant RelayView tools into competitors as a required experiment.
398	No new memory, probe, expert, code-intelligence or ablation delivery delays the
399	first Stage A/B baseline. Governance/recovery/human-review benefits need their own
400	deterministic fault-injection evidence or declared human rubric, not coding scores.
401	
402	## Delivery ownership
403	
404	- #18 tracks the two-stage program and its completion identities.
405	- #23 implements stage-aware, variable-arm-set scheduling and resume checks.
406	- #24 prepares the successor Stage A freeze from #219's adoption record,
407	  executes and seals each cohort separately, and owns Stage A seal accounting.
408	- #25 owns the complete screening report/dispositions and the later expansion
409	  report; screening publication does not wait for #66.
410	- #50 owns the Stage B corpus/resource freeze; its historical Stage A freezes
411	  and MultiLang measurement readiness remain preserved records.
412	- #219 owns the full reviewed archive release and its 23-task adoption record.
413	- #62/#64 own RelayView delivery. Closed #65 is historical v4/VnimanieAI
414	  admission; #172 owns the staged-v5 Intel-successor admission required by Stage B.
415	- #128 owns executable v4 reconciliation, #129/#130 standard Pi specification and
416	  admission, #131 outcome dimensions, and #132 later within-RelayView ablations.
417	- #160 owns the v5 Claude Code identity and seven-arm contract amendment; a
418	  separate fresh delivery/admission record must precede any live Claude task.
419	- #66 owns Stage B RelayView checkpoint analysis only.
420	- #68 and #70–#73 retain historical declared research delivery/admission evidence.
421	  #112–#116 own the GitHub-excluded successor policy, implementation, legacy-six-arm
422	  integration and fresh admission. #98–#102 remain historical public-web
423	  qualification evidence and cannot admit the successor cohort.
424	
425	The [delivery roadmap](unified-benchmark-roadmap.md) translates these rules into
426	issue-specific acceptance changes. Executable successor schemas, fixtures, adapter and
427	scheduler enforcement must be delivered and tested before a freeze can authorize
428	live trials; v1–v4 validation artifacts must not be relabeled as v5 compliance.

# Staged MultiLang benchmark contract v5 — product comparison and attribution

Status: implemented prospective freeze contract, owner-approved design 2026-09-14. Successor to
[v4](staged-multilang-benchmark-v4.md), preserving its corpus, outcome and
[GitHub-excluded policy](github-excluded-research-v1.md). This document is not an
actual numerical freeze or permission to run a cohort. The
[`staged-multilang-benchmark/5`](../../schemas/staged-benchmark-v5.schema.json)
schema, [offline validator](../../scripts/validate_staged_contract_v5.py), and
[Stage A](../../fixtures/staged-v5/stage-a.json)/[Stage B](../../fixtures/staged-v5/stage-b.json)
fixtures implement #160's seven-arm amendment. The [orthogonal task outcome
v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md) implements #131's prospective fields. Existing
v1–v4 artifacts retain their identities.
Stage A corpus amendment (amended 2026-10-03,
[ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)):
Stage A screens the 23 reviewed archive tasks bound to the full archive
release, every Stage A count below is derived from the frozen corpus, and the
cohort runs all blocks continuously under one admitted configuration. The
validator, scheduler, launcher, audit and seal enforce this through the
`archive-stage-a-cohort/1` execution scope; the [continuous-cohort
runbook](../runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md) describes its operation.

## Executable freeze boundary

One v5 manifest is the complete effective freeze for exactly one stage. It names
the stage and finite cohort window; exact arm, role, runtime, model, provider,
authentication, endpoint, reasoning, prompt/tool artifact paths and hashes, and
admission identities;
the shared-broker/GitHub-excluded policy and its deviation disclosure; exact
corpus tasks, source revisions, environments, verifier/scorer and resources;
deadlines, repetitions, attempts, exact shared-research limits, provider/account
reservations, local compute, retry and analysis policies; the seeded complete
schedule and its deterministic arm/task/attempt slot plan; owner approval; and
the complete task outcome v2 artifact/policy/slot-plan identity. The shared
research account ceilings are the current `shared-research-budget/2` values:
360 calls, 120 provider attempts and 120 fetched documents. Whole-manifest canonical identity is the
resume boundary: changing any field is incompatible.

Stage A validation permits exactly the seven standard arms and no post-outcome
survivor information. Stage B embeds a content-addressed Stage A capability
disposition containing exactly one classification for each scheduled Stage A
slot (161 under the current 23-task corpus). Validation binds that artifact to
the sealed Stage A freeze and outcome slot plan, applies the futility gate
independently to each arm's slots (one per Stage A task), and
derives its only legal survivor set rather than trusting a separately authored
list. It then requires both RelayView arms plus
the model-neutral `pi-standard` identity, yielding three through ten arms. #129
freezes that arm's exact model/provider route before admission. Product-native Codex,
OpenCode, Claude Code and Pi profiles remain single-agent; only RelayView may declare its
planner/implementer/reviewer workflow profile. Every arm binds
`github-excluded-v1` with native search disabled. Reserved RelayView tool names
and categories cannot be relabeled as product-native capabilities, and the local
implementer's GPU/concurrency identity must match the compute envelope. Stage B
carries the Stage A freeze digest, corpus identity, task IDs, outcome-seal-backed
capability disposition and canonical disjointness evidence. An executable Stage B validation additionally requires
the sealed Stage A manifest through `--stage-a-freeze`, its independently
recorded canonical digest through `--trusted-stage-a-freeze-digest`, the
published disposition digest through `--trusted-stage-a-disposition-digest`,
and the source outcome-seal digest through
`--trusted-stage-a-outcome-seal-digest`. It rejects any freeze, disposition,
seal, identity, task-list or corpus mismatch, and the scheduler retains all four
trust inputs as resume identity.
Synthetic fixtures exercise the wire contract. Executable Stage B validation
also requires a fresh exact-arm Pi record through `--pi-admission`; missing or
invalid evidence blocks the run without removing Pi from the arm set. Stage A is
independent of this gate. The validator still never authorizes execution by
itself: `--for-execution` remains fail-closed until #50 evidence and #23/#24
enforcement exist.
Issue #24 must supply the Stage A `purpose=freeze` manifest on the reviewed
archive-bound corpus (23 tasks, ADR-0016), and #50 the later disjoint Stage B
corpus. Each needs exact admitted identities and real approval/evidence digests
before #23/#24 may consume it.

## Purpose and fair product comparison

The primary benchmark supports honest product marketing: how recognizable developer
configurations compare on coding outcomes, latency and resources. RelayView may be
valuable by preserving coding quality while adding separately demonstrated
governance, provenance, safe recovery and human-review benefits. No AGI claim or
unexplained composite score follows from this experiment.

Fairness means identical task/scorer inputs and disclosed, prospectively frozen
conditions—not identical tools. Preserve each product's useful native capabilities
and equivalents. Do not transplant RelayView-specialized memory, AST/LSP/code
intelligence, expert escalation, separate planner/implementer roles or auto-review
into Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code or standard Pi just to equalize them. Do not cripple competing
products by removing native equivalents.

The shared broker, disabled native research routes and GitHub-family exclusions
are deliberate controls that change the native experience. Report them; do not
claim these are untouched stock profiles. This amendment does not undo those
controls, change normal non-benchmark defaults or permit ad hoc source exceptions.

## Invariants

- A cohort is identified by immutable corpus, arm-set, policy, scheduler, scorer
  and resource digests. Resume rejects any mismatch.
- Every task input, source/setup revision, environment image digest, verifier and
  scorer is identical across the arms in that cohort.
- One trial is one arm-task-repetition slot. Every scheduled slot is reconciled as
  valid capability evidence, infrastructure missing, unsupported or unstarted.
- Primary task outcome incorporates eligible within-budget delivery and independent
  terminal-candidate verification. Preserve the verifier observation separately:
  an eligible task timeout remains primary zero even if a retained patch passes.
  Automated/human dispositions are separate; initial/reviewed RelayView candidates
  are paired secondary checkpoints, not additional arms.
- Capability results never select or replace tasks. Hidden verifier material and
  scores remain unavailable until automatic work has stopped and cannot feed a
  later role or retry.
- Research profiles, model/provider routes, prompts, deadlines, attempts and
  budgets are frozen prospectively. The shared research budget v2 applies. All
  seven Stage A arms use the controlled researcher under
  [`github-excluded-v1`](github-excluded-research-v1.md); public-web or native
  search evidence does not admit this cohort.
- Screening, expansion, pilot, shakedown and conformance evidence are never pooled.

## Stage A — screening cohort

The arm set is exactly the seven standard arms listed in ADR-0012. RelayView is not
part of this cohort and its delivery or admission cannot block Stage A.

The seventh arm is `claude-code-claude-opus-5`, frozen by the
[Claude Code subscription baseline](../authoritative/claude-code-subscription-baseline.md).
It uses Claude Code 2.1.270, full-name `claude-opus-5`, high effort, the Anthropic
subscription route, native prompt and repository instruction discovery, one
primary coding agent, an exact native tool inventory, and only the controlled
research MCP pair. The `Agent`, `Workflow`, agent-team, native web/search and
alternate research paths are disabled. Any alias, fallback, package, route,
tool, prompt-discovery, output, deadline or retry drift creates a different arm.

Every Stage A launcher explicitly selects `--github-excluded`. The default
`public-web-v1` remains available for non-benchmark work but is inadmissible for
this cohort. Codex/GPT-5.6 Sol disables native OpenAI search only in its generated
benchmark profile and receives the same broker tools as the other six arms. All
six legacy arms require fresh live admission under issue #116 before task delivery;
the Claude arm requires its own fresh exact-identity admission before task delivery. Historical
#73/#98-#102 evidence remains operational history rather than current admission.
The immutable seven-record index binds the exact retained matrix, per-arm evidence,
deployment/setup identities and common controlled-service identity. A Stage A
freeze records that index as `source_policy.research_admission_digest`; changing
or omitting it creates an incompatible freeze and blocks dispatch.

Issue #50 selected 25 validated tasks from a content-addressed revision of
`SWE-bench-Live/MultiLang`; the executable Stage A corpus is the reviewed
subset of that selection defined below. The current candidate dataset revision is
`62dc0745c40f067fc366ae3eb1a26136e5928f85`; #50 must independently verify it and
must not substitute a mutable branch or `latest` reference. Candidate tasks have
`created_at >= 2026-04-01`, after #50 verifies whether that field represents the
source issue or pull-request time and records the underlying source timestamp.
At that candidate revision the date filter yields 512 rows (C 77, C++ 100, Go 36,
JavaScript 22, Rust 101, Java 81, TypeScript 15 and C# 80); #50 must reproduce the
inventory before treating it as freeze input.

The selection algorithm is frozen before capability outcomes:

1. Validate eligibility, environment reproducibility, base/no-op behavior, the
   gold patch repeatedly, verifier isolation, problem/test alignment and the
   supported host/resource envelope.
2. Freeze the exact selection allocation. The original was `c=3`, `cpp=3`,
   `go=3`, `js=3`, `rust=3`, `java=3`, `ts=3`, `cs=4`; the selection that
   produced the archived tasks used ADR-0015's `c=3`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`, `js=3`,
   `rust=3`, `java=0`, `ts=4`, `cs=4`.
3. Within each language, retain only the newest eligible task per repository,
   then order tasks by the ISO `created_at` value descending and `instance_id`
   ascending using bytewise comparison. Select the allocation from the head of
   each order. The selected tasks must come from distinct repositories.
4. Freeze the remaining per-language order as the replacement list. A replacement
   stays in the same language and uses the next unused repository. It is allowed
   only for a predeclared validation failure discovered before any comparative
   outcome, never for difficulty or an arm outcome, and creates a new corpus
   revision. After the first trial begins, no task replacement is permitted.
   A task that later leaves the eligible set is dropped, not replaced; the
   change creates a new corpus identity and a smaller schedule.

The executable Stage A corpus is the reviewed subset of the full task-archive
release: 23 tasks from 23 repositories, allocation `c=2`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`,
`js=3`, `rust=2`, `java=0`, `ts=4`, `cs=4`. Archive review left
`AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` and `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180` `unresolved`; both are
dropped without replacement. Each retained task keeps its selected task ID,
source revision and task text and is graded by its reviewed validator. Reports
disclose the reduced C and Rust strata and the absence of Java.

MultiLang does not publish a separate per-row ingestion timestamp. #50 must prove
the semantics and normalization of `created_at` before it becomes the recency key;
if that proof fails, the freeze is blocked pending a new owner decision. Applied
to the unvalidated pinned inventory, this rule's projected oldest selected value
is `2026-04-17T03:18:51Z` (`danielmiessler__Fabric-2098`, Go). The projection is
planning evidence, not a frozen task: validation may move the final oldest date
earlier while preserving the exact language and repository allocation.

The MultiLang adapter is part of the measuring instrument and must consume each
task's declared rebuild/test/print commands, log parser and image. It must discover
the repository root rather than assume `/testbed/.git`, safely isolate untrusted
parser/test execution, support compiled-language resource needs, pin images by
digest and emit typed failures. Existing Python/Inspect scorer evidence does not
admit this adapter. #50 records the exact adapter, evaluator and schema versions
and fresh validation evidence.

The scheduler creates seeded task/repetition blocks containing exactly all seven
arms. It may execute sequentially and may defer a quota-blocked slot within a
block, but cannot omit it or begin a later block early.

Stage A runs every block in schedule order from one ledger under one admitted
configuration and the owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of that freeze
is the only launch decision. The cohort has no first-block stop and no owner
go/no-go between blocks. Each block runs under the admitted per-block
supervisor watchdog. After a block completes cleanly, the launcher
automatically starts the next block from the same ledger under the same
supervisor policy, with no operator action. A block that does not complete
cleanly, including a watchdog stop, stops the cohort fail-closed. An uncertain
or active attempt is never replayed, the ledger is never reset, and an
infrastructure stop retains the ledger and evidence for diagnosis. Resuming
the same ledger requires the same admitted configuration and is a recovery,
not a new approval.

The Claude arm's enrollment receipt must cover each pending Claude turn under
the frozen phase limits. An authenticated renewal during the run is a recorded
operator recovery, not an owner decision. It keeps the same account, token,
tier and credit/isolation settings and authenticates against the frozen
identities. It carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation and adds no
reservation or refund. It never extends or overwrites the original receipt,
and it is bound into the ledger and evidence. Without a valid renewal, a
pending turn the receipt cannot cover fails closed before reservation, and a
renewal with a changed identity is rejected.

After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit covers
all scheduled slots, including every renewal's chronology, before #24 seals
the cohort. The historical #155 and #220 first-block executions keep their own
stop, audit and owner decisions.

The freeze declares
repetitions, the common total workflow deadline, retry policy, concurrency and
per-provider/account/local-compute reservations. Stage A freezes exactly one
repetition: one trial per arm-task pair, so the schedule has the frozen task
count × seven slots (161 for 23 tasks). This directional
screen identifies critically failing arms; it does not estimate run-to-run
reliability. A study of multiple tries requires a separately identified cohort,
predeclared aggregation and interpretation, and results that are not pooled with
Stage A.

## Screening report and futility disposition

Issue #24 seals Stage A independently. Issue #25 publishes all seven arms with
scheduled, attempted, valid, unsupported, infrastructure-missing and unstarted
denominators; per-task outcomes; all-scheduled lower/upper bounds; task-clustered
uncertainty; failure-inclusive time; research/provider/local resource use; and all
predeclared paired comparisons. It must say that one task is 1/23 of an arm's
denominator, about 4.35 percentage points, and must not present close ordering
as a precise ranking. Before publishing
the trusted disposition digest, #25 must validate each disposition record against
the independently trusted Stage A outcome seal and the sealed outcome records; the
Stage B validator authenticates both that published disposition and its referenced
source seal, but does not reinterpret the outcome records itself.

No fixed number of arms is dropped. A standard arm is capability-futile only when

`resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`

after every one of its 23 scheduled task slots is reconciled. `capability_unknown`
includes every slot whose missingness could conceal a resolution. The rule is an
absolute resource stop, not statistical proof of general inferiority. An arm with
an upper bound of at least 2/23 survives. Failure to achieve frozen admission or
minimum valid coverage after the predeclared bounded attempts is reported as
`unsupported` and decided separately; it must not be described as capability
culling. Every disposition and its inputs are sealed as
`stage-a-capability-disposition/1`: one ordered record per scheduled Stage A
slot (161), carrying the frozen slot
ID, arm ID and one of `resolved`, `not_resolved`, `capability_unknown` or
`unstarted`, plus the Stage A freeze, outcome slot-plan and source outcome-seal
digests. The same calculation is performed independently for each of the seven
arms, including Claude Code; it cannot be omitted from the disposition input or
treated as an automatic survivor.

## Stage B — selected-arm expansion cohort

After the Stage A seal and report, #50 freezes a new corpus containing no Stage A
task. Prefer repository-disjointness from Stage A and development/shakedown exposure
where feasible, freeze exclusions before outcomes, and disclose unavoidable overlap.
The arm set is every surviving standard arm plus `relayview-sol`, `relayview-local`
and one standard single-agent Pi baseline under newly frozen exact identities.
RelayView production delivery (#64), Intel-successor exact-pair admission (#172), research readiness
(#68) and Pi adapter/admission (#130) gate Stage B only. A material configuration change to a
standard arm requires a new name and admission; it is not the same continuing arm.

The owner freezes Stage B sample size, language/repository allocation, practical
thresholds, repetitions, resources and exact arm set after seeing the complete
Stage A report but before any Stage B outcome. Stage A may inform those prospective
choices. Stage B task selection may use only frozen metadata and validation, not
which Stage A tasks or arms succeeded. The cohort is described as
`<N>-arm selected expansion`, with three through ten arms; it is ten-arm only
when all seven standard arms survive. Standard Pi must not be silently omitted if
admission is unavailable: an altered arm set needs a new explicit owner decision.

Issue #23 schedules the exact frozen Stage B arm set. #24 produces a separate seal.
#25 produces a separate expansion report and does not combine numerators,
denominators or uncertainty with Stage A. It discloses the selection procedure and
limits generalization accordingly. #66 analyzes RelayView's paired checkpoints
only from the Stage B seal and supplies that secondary analysis to the expansion
report.

## Standard single-agent Pi

[#129](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/129) pins the
[standard single-agent Pi baseline](../authoritative/pi-standard-baseline.md): Pi
0.85.0, `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`, ChatGPT OAuth, high reasoning, native prompt
and instruction discovery, one RPC-controlled agent, all seven Pi built-in coding
and search/list tools, and only the controlled research pair as a non-native
extension. [#130](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/130)
implements and admits that exact identity. No extra Pi-local arm is implicitly
approved.

The capability inventory covers file read/edit/write, text/file search, shell,
tests/builds, interruption/deadlines/output bounds, repository instructions,
native context handling, provider features and admitted research. Distinguish native
tools, necessary benchmark capture/isolation/research adapters, optional commonplace
extensions and RelayView-specific enhancements. A practical baseline is not a claim
of identical capabilities or an intentionally weakened agent.

Stage B prospectively freezes the existing shared-broker/GitHub-excluded treatment
for every selected arm, including Pi and RelayView, with fresh exact-policy admission.
Do not reinterpret old native/public-web evidence as admission. One workflow budget
covers every role/continuation/retry; reviewer research remains zero under the
existing policy. No additional memory/code-intelligence/assistance allowance is
introduced.

## Outcome dimensions and evaluator integrity

The implemented prospective [task outcome v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md) versions
verifier result, terminal reason, delivery-within-budget, primary task outcome/score
and applicable automated/human dispositions separately. The
[implemented timeout policy](../authoritative/task-budget-outcomes.md) remains:
eligible active-agent deadline timeout is primary zero, terminal and non-retryable.
A passing retained patch may separately have verifier pass. Setup/auth/provider/
capture/scorer failures and manual cancellation are not invented test failures.
Unknown identity/usage remains unknown. Specify combined-cause precedence and
eligibility deterministically before execution.

Preserve upstream task/tests/evaluator semantics. #50 validates local integration
using repeated gold and base/no-op controls, the same patch through upstream and
integrated paths where feasible, correct rebuild instead of stale compiled output,
test discovery, setup/parser failures and candidate test tampering. Reuse existing
coverage. Supplemental behavioral tests are separately labeled diagnostics, never
silent changes to the official score.

Historical logs, seals and original interpretations stay immutable. Any offline
reinterpretation identifies both original and successor policy; preserve the
disclosed after-observation adoption of the existing timeout policy.

## Reporting, generalization and resource limits

#25 publishes predeclared paired wins/losses, task-clustered uncertainty,
scheduled/attempted/valid/missing denominators, all-scheduled bounds and
failure-inclusive latency. Repetitions are not new independent repositories.
A 23-task screen changes about 4.35 percentage points per task; zero to four
examples per language cannot support language rankings. Recency-first selection is purposive,
not random; resampling does not cure that limitation. Dates do not establish
absence from pretraining, public mirrors or developer tuning.

Disclose Stage A-informed selection/sizing and Stage B repository/development
overlap; describe familiar/new repositories separately when overlap is unavoidable.
“No significant difference” does not establish no degradation. Confirmatory
non-inferiority requires a predeclared tolerable margin, comparison, uncertainty
criterion and adequate sample/resources. Inconclusive results remain publishable.

Freeze actual versus unavailable token/output/turn enforcement, all-role/provider
and research usage, workflow deadlines and local CPU/GPU/memory/concurrency limits.
Report cold/warm provisioning/cache effects and unknown metrics. Equal wall time
is not equal compute; subscription use is neither zero cost nor grounds for
inventing a per-task API price. Preserve account counters and reservations.
A finite cohort window, bounded operational attempts and resource-stop rules
prevent indefinite waiting. Unsupported admission is not capability-futility.
The retained upper-bound rule (at most one possible resolution, 1/23) is
near-total-failure screening, not a precise inferiority test or economical
arm-ranking procedure.

GitHub exclusions block legitimate documentation including GitHub Pages and do not
prevent every solution exposure. Retain sanitized denial/filter diagnostics, not
blocked source content, and label restricted-source conditions. A realistic-docs
sensitivity cohort is optional later work, not a post-results exception.

## Later feature attribution

[#132](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/132) owns a
separate held-out RelayView-only ablation study after the first product baseline,
consuming [RelayView #446](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/pi-coding-agent-setup/issues/446).
Design may proceed earlier. Use a stripped RelayView control and prioritized
feature-specific contrasts as features ship; distinguish incremental from
full-minus-one designs and record interactions. Feature-off must remove execution/
tool admission and isolate mutable state. Reject impossible combinations or name
them as compound interventions; planner removal may alter reviewer snapshots too.

Control task/model routes and total budgets, with comparable extra self-work where
feasible for review attribution. Initial/reviewed checkpoints alone measure
review-plus-correction, additional work and selection—not a reviewer-only causal
effect. Publish regressions and missingness. Hidden scores never guide agents,
escalation, retry or candidate choice.

Do not transplant RelayView tools into competitors as a required experiment.
No new memory, probe, expert, code-intelligence or ablation delivery delays the
first Stage A/B baseline. Governance/recovery/human-review benefits need their own
deterministic fault-injection evidence or declared human rubric, not coding scores.

## Delivery ownership

- #18 tracks the two-stage program and its completion identities.
- #23 implements stage-aware, variable-arm-set scheduling and resume checks.
- #24 prepares the successor Stage A freeze from #219's adoption record,
  executes and seals each cohort separately, and owns Stage A seal accounting.
- #25 owns the complete screening report/dispositions and the later expansion
  report; screening publication does not wait for #66.
- #50 owns the Stage B corpus/resource freeze; its historical Stage A freezes
  and MultiLang measurement readiness remain preserved records.
- #219 owns the full reviewed archive release and its 23-task adoption record.
- #62/#64 own RelayView delivery. Closed #65 is historical v4/VnimanieAI
  admission; #172 owns the staged-v5 Intel-successor admission required by Stage B.
- #128 owns executable v4 reconciliation, #129/#130 standard Pi specification and
  admission, #131 outcome dimensions, and #132 later within-RelayView ablations.
- #160 owns the v5 Claude Code identity and seven-arm contract amendment; a
  separate fresh delivery/admission record must precede any live Claude task.
- #66 owns Stage B RelayView checkpoint analysis only.
- #68 and #70–#73 retain historical declared research delivery/admission evidence.
  #112–#116 own the GitHub-excluded successor policy, implementation, legacy-six-arm
  integration and fresh admission. #98–#102 remain historical public-web
  qualification evidence and cannot admit the successor cohort.

The [delivery roadmap](unified-benchmark-roadmap.md) translates these rules into
issue-specific acceptance changes. Executable successor schemas, fixtures, adapter and
scheduler enforcement must be delivered and tested before a freeze can authorize
live trials; v1–v4 validation artifacts must not be relabeled as v5 compliance.

# Unattended cohort execution: the attempt-3 stop and its fixes

## Status

Implemented in the harness for #271. The provider-free on-host rehearsal
result is recorded below. Attempt 3 is retired and attempt 4 is prepared only
after this change merges and asrock is re-admitted at its commit.

## The stop

Cohort attempt 3 on `cachyos-asrock` used freeze
`sha256:735f29e099a98b88ac982c891f9516ebaa50be6617c643aa06683363ff2e889b`,
which binds the admitted host profile
`sha256:5d890be13e19e9076558d4927af4c49704ad7d84a3b81b426d375cd55b4315e9` at
commit `97d18ae`. It launched at 2026-10-06T17:03:35Z as the supervised unit
`agent-evals-host-2976c9f832a744e048e913ff`.

- **The stop.** The unit stopped at 17:34:56Z on its first slot,
  `opencode-glm-5.3` × `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`. The worker resolved the Z.AI key
  through `vault_session.unlock`, whose `getpass` raised `GetPassWarning`,
  because a systemd unit has no terminal.
- **What the ledger holds.** The reservation had been committed eleven seconds
  earlier. The ledger now holds one `in_flight` slot and 160 `pending`, and
  the attempt directory holds only `intent.json` and `interrupted.json`.
- **No requests were made.** The research sidecar and the agent container
  start after credential delivery, so no provider or research request was
  made.
- **Evidence retained.**
  - On the host: the unit journal and unit state, beside the attempt directory.
  - Off host: `cohort-attempt-3-launch-1-stop/evidence.tar`,
    `sha256:c13ee9a05ae8bbdfc891387f7cc0da780f552c784b6ee85ac504d51796e9ae43`.

## Why tests did not catch it

No test had run the live worker's credential path in a process without a
terminal:

- the execution tests replace `run_native`;
- the vault tests replace `getpass`;
- the runbook test's interpreter shim reported `isatty()` as true for every
  command, including the one its stand-in `systemd-run` started.

A read-only audit of the live path found these further defects, which would
have stopped or corrupted the cohort later:

- the provider-free launch preflight must run inside the admitted supervisor
  unit;
- the launch did not clear the unit name that host qualification leaves
  loaded (#270);
- resume did not clear a failed unit;
- the two ChatGPT arms received a refresh-disabled token with no lifetime
  check sized to the attempt (`CodexChatGPTCredential()` checked 0 s,
  OpenCode 390 s). An access token lasts 10 days
  ([evidence](stage-a-codex-renewal-staged-50-20260920.json)), and an expired
  one would have been recorded as the arm's authentication failure.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-06, Claude Code session)

- **Fix and re-run.** "Please fix that we need to rerun the stopped slot and
  Yeah, we'll readmit as well just try to make sure everything's fixed this
  time before we go through the whole process of re-admitting and resetting
  up everything." Attempt 3 is retired: its ledger, artifact root and
  task-input store move into its own attempt directory, and the next attempt's
  freeze runs that slot as a fresh slot.
- **One Claude confirmation per cohort.** "While we're doing this, can we make
  the Claude side use a one-year token also? I don't want to have to check in
  every day and refresh it." The Claude arm already uses the one-year setup
  token. What was daily is the owner's account-policy confirmation, then
  capped at 24 hours. The step-12 confirmation now lasts until the approved
  cohort window ends, at most 35 days (the research admission ceiling).
  - Its statement records the owner's undertaking to stop the cohort if the
    account policy changes.
  - Nothing re-checks that policy during the window.
  - Every Claude turn still checks the delivered token against the receipt.

## What changed

- **Provider credential lease.** Step 2's single masked unlock exports the
  Brave key and the four provider attachments (Claude setup token, Z.AI key,
  Meta key, Codex ChatGPT login) to private files on `/dev/shm`. A manifest
  binds each file to the admitted vault's digest. The live worker reads only
  this lease, and a missing or changed lease stops the run.
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before each reservation the launcher
  runs the next slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact boundary,
  with nothing reserved:
  - credential delivery and a ChatGPT access lifetime of at least 4,020 s;
  - Claude's token against the covering receipt;
  - the research service start and stop;
  - the sandbox and observer definition.

  It then tears all of this down before the Inspect evaluation would start. A
  failure stops the cohort with the slot pending, and a resume runs it.
- **Runbook.**
  - Step 0 refreshes the ChatGPT login before admission.
  - The launch preflight runs in the admitted unit with `systemd-run --wait`.
  - The launch inspects and clears a finished unit of the same name first.
  - A resume clears a failed unit.
  - A stopped attempt is retired before a new one, and both leases are
    removed at the end.
- **Runbook test.** The stand-in `systemd-run` gives its command `/dev/null`
  as stdin, and the shim makes any prompt inside a unit fail. The fixture
  worker and rehearsal deliver credentials from the exported lease.
- **On-host rehearsal.** `scripts/rehearse_stage_a_unattended.py` rehearses
  every arm inside a real `systemd-run` unit under the cohort's limits and
  `env -i` environment, from the candidate checkout and before re-admission,
  using an existing freeze and a copy of the research state.

## On-host rehearsal

Run on 2026-10-06 on `cachyos-asrock`, from a clean clone of this branch at
`930d72b` with `uv sync --locked`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and the staged
checkout's pinned Muse Codex build (`vendor/codex-muse/runtime`, which git does
not track) copied in. The owner exported both leases with
`rehearse_stage_a_unattended.py export` in one masked unlock, pinned to the
admitted vault digest `sha256:4450416b…c2df` (`provider_attachments=4`).

The `run` subcommand ran in the transient unit
`stage-a-unattended-rehearsal-271`:

- **Limits and environment.** `CPUQuota=100%`, `MemoryMax=2147483648`,
  `TasksMax=128`, `RuntimeMaxSec=105780`, `Nice=10`, with `env -i`
  `PATH=<runtime path>` `LANG` `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and no terminal.
- **Inputs.** Attempt 3's freeze and configuration, the retained
  `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367` image, and a copy of the research state.

Results:

- **First run.** Six arms passed. `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` failed
  with `Muse Codex runtime inventory changed` because the clone lacked the
  untracked Muse build.
- **Second run.** The rerun first needed `systemctl --user reset-failed`,
  which the runbook's resume step now documents. Receipt `rehearsal.json`
  `sha256:d3a66b1779218a3abdc27019bdb0e4bbf86823540ec0228bddd7aaeaac15ae7a`:
  - `status=passed`, with host bwrap passed;
  - every arm (`codex-gpt-5.6-sol`, `codex-glm-5.3`,
    `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `opencode-gpt-5.6-sol`,
    `opencode-glm-5.3`, `opencode-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`,
    `claude-code-claude-opus-5`) reached the provider-contact boundary and
    confirmed cleanup;
  - the cgroup was confirmed at the supervisor limits, and the unit's memory
    peak was 1,029,058,560 bytes (of 2 GiB);
  - service runtime 67 s, `provider_requests=0`.

  This exercised, for every arm:
  - delivery from the provider lease;
  - the ChatGPT access lifetime check (the vault's token outlives a
    4,020 s attempt);
  - the Claude token against its receipt;
  - the research worker scope started from inside the unit;
  - the sandbox and observer definition on the evaluation daemon.

  Afterwards no trial container, network, research or rehearsal unit, or
  scratch directory remained, and the conserved research ledger was
  unchanged.

After the two-axis review, the code changed:

- each slot rehearsal runs its research service on a copy of the research
  state;
- a ChatGPT token must outlive the live check by the 480 s rehearsal margin;
- the step-3 receipt keeps its 24-hour cap;
- the lease is hardened, and its module is renamed `stage_a_provider_credentials`.

The rehearsal was rerun at `cb8b978`, the last code commit, with the same
leases and inputs. Receipt
`sha256:330c1729173dcef845d6f0a96574b1d58e3d16e4832dade4e077e3ae008769c9`:

- `status=passed`, with all seven arms and host bwrap passed;
- memory peak 1,028,513,792 bytes, service runtime 61 s.

Afterwards there were no containers or research units, and the conserved
`research.sqlite` was unmodified since 2026-10-06T08:00:27-04:00.

## Retirement of attempt 3

Retired on 2026-10-06, after the rehearsal and before re-admission, by the
owner's decision above.

- **First try.** The block from #271 stopped at its image release (`an
  attempt still holds the task image`), because the store refuses changes while
  the ledger at the admitted path holds an in-flight slot. Nothing had moved;
  only an empty `retired` directory existed.
- **Second try (#273).** Run in the corrected order: the ledger moved first,
  then the release (`status=released`, `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`), then the artifact
  root. Results:
  - `state/stage-a/cohort-stage-a-reviewed-23-v1-attempt-3/retired/` holds
    `scheduler.json`, still
    `sha256:7b4f4a967d8a3f03329806d9a9a8fd5e870e20127039241f7dfa435a2d77cc41`,
    the hash at the stop, and `live/`;
  - an empty artifact root is in place.

## ChatGPT refresh before re-admission (#275)

The owner refreshed the Codex ChatGPT login in asrock's vault on 2026-10-06
at about 16:30 EDT, with the broker runbook's procedure and the pinned Codex
0.144.0. The vault moved from the owner-steps chain head
`4450416b3550c4b8d4f0fee331eda81efda6495de2b2c0a31e2d41bc2d5ec2df`, the Brave
enrollment's result and the admitted pin, to
`c3114764badccccee91fa8c6ba1534140f4e6bdfc27ed7abb8828635be62eb0b`.

The previous login dated from 2026-10-04T19:00Z, so its token would have
expired around 2026-10-14. The new one lasts until about 2026-10-16.

The owner-steps chain could not record a change after its last enrollment, and
plan building requires the Brave chain to reach the admitted vault. #275 adds
the same-account rotation record, and the refresh is recorded with it before
re-admission.

100	## Stop: a lost `exec_remote` job (#283)
101	
102	### Status
103	
104	Fixed by #283: a lost native process is now a recorded outcome, not a stop.
105	That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
106	attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
107	(retries) was declined. The reasons:
108	
109	- **A lost slot can't wrongly cut an arm.** It counts as
110	  `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
111	- **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
112	  corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
113	- **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
114	  baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.
115	
116	#293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
117	process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
118	outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
119	so that the next failure can name its trigger.
120	
121	The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
122	a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
123	Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.
124	
125	### The stop
126	
127	The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
128	in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
129	`native/inspect.json`.
130	
131	- **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
132	  actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
133	  `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
134	  `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
135	- **What failed.**
136	  - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
137	    10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
138	  - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
139	    failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
140	  - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
141	    as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
142	    10:56:47.89Z.
143	- **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
144	  Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
145	  complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
146	  unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
147	- **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
148	  remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.
149	
150	### Mechanism
151	
152	Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):
153	
154	- **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
155	  `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
156	  exec, up to twice.
157	- **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
158	  as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
159	  jobs.
160	- **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
161	  final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
162	  `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.
163	
164	The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
165	for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
166	from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.
167	
168	**The retained evidence contradicts it.**
169	- **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
170	  (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from
171	  10:53:51Z, 1–14 seconds apart, through the supposed hang. The last one is at
172	  10:56:47.428Z, after the kill was sent.
173	- **So the job could not have been retired as finished.** A job is retired
174	  only after its process exits, and pid 428 was Codex itself: `/bin/sh -c`,
175	  `env` and `sh -c 'exec "$@"'` all `exec`.
176	
177	**The server was most likely replaced while Codex ran.** Read from the same
178	pinned source:
179	- **The client restarts a server it can't reach.** Before every call, the
180	  sandbox-tools client checks the server's socket in `/tmp/sandbox-tools/`. If
181	  it cannot reach it, it starts a new server with an empty job registry.
182	- **The old job runs on.** Jobs are plain children of the old server, so they
183	  keep running as orphans.
184	- **This fits the stop.** The kill was answered by a live server, with a
185	  JSON-RPC error rather than a transport failure. Codex kept calling the
186	  provider until the container was removed.
187	
188	**The trigger is unconfirmed.** The adapter kept none of Codex's stream. The
189	candidates are all within the agent's reach:
190	- **Killing the server.** The agent runs as the same user as the server, in one
191	  process namespace, with Codex's own sandbox bypassed.
192	- **Removing its state.** The server's socket and pid file are on the agent's
193	  64 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs.
194	- **A server crash.** The host showed no OOM.
195	
196	**Settling it next time.** From #296 on, a lost process records, before
197	teardown, the server identified when the job started and whether it is still
198	alive, the current server, the state directory's listing and the tail of
199	`server-stderr.log`. A different current server confirms a replacement, and
200	the partial stream that #283 persists shows the agent's last commands.
201	
202	### Prevention: agents run unprivileged
203	
204	The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (#296) that every arm's agent will run as an
205	unprivileged user, with the sandbox-tools server out of its reach. Running all
206	arms at the same privilege level also keeps the comparison even. Today every
207	arm's agent runs as the container's root user, like the server; only Claude
208	Code's MCP bridge drops to another user. The change is tracked separately
209	(#300); until it lands, a failure is recorded and the agent stopped, but
210	not prevented.
211	
212	### Retry-log check
213	
214	The owner inspected the interrupted sample's `native/inspect.json` once asrock
215	was reachable again. It holds no `logger` events, only 44 `sandbox` events,
216	spans, `sample_init` and the error. Polls run under `no_events()`, so the
217	transcript can neither confirm nor rule out a `Retrying docker compose command
218	after TimeoutError` re-run.
219	
220	From #283 on, the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll. The native stream

## Lost candidates: httrack capture after an in-tree build (#282)

Fixed by #282 ([ADR 0021](../authoritative/adr/0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md),

### Orders 15–20

The six arms were `opencode-gpt-5.6-sol`, `opencode-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`,
`codex-glm-5.3`, `opencode-glm-5.3`, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` and
`codex-gpt-5.6-sol`. Each native run completed (`terminal.state=completed`, no
adapter failure). Each arm followed httrack's `AGENTS.md` and built in tree,
and each candidate was recorded `candidate_capture_failed`.

The capture's reason was not persisted, but each native `inspect.json` keeps

```text
RepositorySanitizationError: edits inside submodule cannot be represented safely: src/coucal; changed paths: [".deps", ...]
```

`src/proxytrack`, `src/*/.dirstamp`, and `tests/*.log` with `tests/*.trs`.

([ADR 0022](../authoritative/adr/0022-retain-archive-grades-whose-test-names-are-secret-shaped.md)):
an archive grade persists every status with each name redacted.

### Orders 22–28

All seven arms exported a candidate, and the hidden tests ran. Each
`verification/inspect-error.json` reads:

```json
{"error_type": "UnsafeArtifactError", "message": "redaction produced duplicate artifact keys"}
```

The grade keys 26,864 statuses by test name. Two of them,
`github.com/github/gh-aw/pkg/stringutil/TestSpec_PublicAPI_ClassifyPAT/ghp__prefix_yields_classic`
and `.../gho__prefix_yields_oauth`, match the GitHub-token pattern and redacted

names unredacted, which the result-root secret scan would also reject.

Replayed through the fixed boundary, order 24's retained grade keeps all
26,864 statuses. The two names persist as `.../[REDACTED]` and
`.../[REDACTED]#2`, and nothing secret-shaped remains.

## Why image qualification missed both (#282)

task:
